motions.title: Full intelligence is the CPU, not the LLM -- wire the CPU path so no task depends on Ollama
motions.description: The voltage doctrine ('the CPU is the intelligence') is already the code's stated design: base_agent.py line 923 says 'Cognitive Microkernel spec: LLM is coprocessor, not CPU'. The intelligence lives in the deterministic interceptor, the Instella MoE microkernel, the K3 fabric, and the skills. But the LLM backend (llm_brain.py -> ollama.chat) is Ollama, and Ollama is stopped by design ('keep Ollama stopped except embedder ingestion'). Any task that falls through the CPU path to the LLM therefore returns '[LLM Offline] Ollama is not running'. Full intelligence means the CPU path (deterministic interceptor + Instella MoE + K3 fabric + skills) must cover EVERY task, so nothing depends on an offline coprocessor. The LLM is a coprocessor to be invoked only when a local model is actually running, never a required path.

motions.title: Raise and measure the agent context window -- 6 turns is why nothing completes
motions.description: base_agent.py line 194 builds the agent's memory context with get_context_window(max_turns=6). The LLM's num_ctx is 16384 (llm_brain.py line 267). A 6-turn memory cap truncates any task chain longer than six exchanges, so a multi-step task loses its earlier context and cannot complete. 'Nothing is completing' is consistent with a context window too short to hold a full task. The context length must be raised and the actual limit measured (memory turns + num_ctx), not asserted from a constant.

motions.title: The agents have tools but the work loop never calls them -- wire task execution, not a tick
motions.description: The agents DO have tools: skills (write_file, read_file, search, shell/run, MCP call_tool), action tags (WRITE_FILE, CREATE_FILES, CALL_TOOL, DELEGATE_TASK, PLAN_FILE), and an autonomous code-test-fix loop (base_agent.py _route_skill + _execute_action_tags). But the kanban agent_work_loop that drives auto-processing advances card lifecycle (TODO->IN_PROGRESS->REVIEW->DONE) + computes a hardware binding, and NEVER invokes process_task -- so cards move but no tool call, no code write, no task happens. The loop must call the assigned agent's process_task (real tool execution) instead of ticking. The tools are present; the dispatcher that should fire them is not.
